'''Susanne Sabine Renner''' is a German [[botanist]]. Until October 2020, she was a professor of biology at [[LMU Munich]] as well as director of the [[Botanische Staatssammlung München]] and the [[Botanical Garden Munich-Nymphenburg|Botanischer Garten München-Nymphenburg]]. Since January 2021, she lives in [[St. Louis]], where she is an Honorary Professor of Biology at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] and a Research Associate at the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]].

==Education ==
Renner received her M.Sc. degree in biology in 1980 and her Ph.D. in 1984, both from the [[University of Hamburg]]. She qualified as Professor in Systematic Botany in 1992.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=April 1, 2017|title=Renner page at University of Missouri St. Louis|url=http://www.umsl.edu/~renners/|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1987 to 1992 Renner was associate professor at the Botanical Institute at the [[Aarhus University]]. From 1993 to 1996, she was Professor at the [[University of Mainz]]. From 1996 to 2006, she was professor at [[University of Missouri–St. Louis]], affiliated with one of the largest botanical gardens worldwide, the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]]. Since 2003, she is professor for systematic botany at [[LMU Munich]] as well as director of the [[Botanische Staatssammlung München]], the [[Botanical Garden Munich-Nymphenburg|Botanischer Garten München-Nymphenburg]] and the University Herbarium (MSB).<ref name=":0" /> As of 2021, she retains an [[emeritus]] position at LMU Munich and is an honorary professor in the [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name=":1">{{cite podcast|url=https://www.sciencefriday.com/segments/where-did-watermelon-come-from/|title=Where Did Watermelon Come From?|website=Science Friday|publisher=|host=Charles Bergquist|date=June 4, 2021|time=|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=gerrity |date=2020-12-30 |title=Susanne S. Renner {{!}} Department of Biology |url=https://biology.wustl.edu/people/susanne-s-renner |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=biology.wustl.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Renner's research interests focus on the [[phylogenetics]], mating system evolution, and [[biogeography]] of flowering plants, in both temperate and tropical regions. ==Awards==
Renner is a member of several notable science academies. In 1999, she was elected to the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref name ="Leopoldina"/> In 2005 she was elected as a foreign member to the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Royal Academy|url=https://www.royalacademy.dk/en/Members/Renner-Susanne-S|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.royalacademy.dk}}</ref> In 2009 she was elected to [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|date=March 2018|title=Leopoldina news|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/uploads/tx_leopublication/Leo_Newsletter_3_2018_ENG_01.pdf|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref> In 2018 she was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Susanne S. Renner|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/susanne-s-renner|access-date=2021-10-05|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> In 2021, she was elected corresponding member of the [[Berlin Society of Friends of Natural Science|Gesellschaft Naturforschender Freunde zu Berlin]] ([https://library.si.edu/donate/adopt-a-book/beschaftigungen-der-berlinischen-gesellschaft-naturforschender-freunde-4-vols founded in 1773]).{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}}
From 2011 to 2020, she was President of the Bavarian Botanical Society.

== Personal life ==
Renner was married to American ornithologist and ecologist [[Robert Ricklefs]] until his death in 2026.<ref>{{citation|title=Profile of Robert E.
